preamble: The palatal lateral [ʎ] can lose its laterality and become the voiced postalveolar fricative [ʒ]. Spanish shows the change twice: in the medieval period, when [ʎ] from Latin -LJ-, -C'L-, -G'L- fricativized to Old Spanish /ʒ/ (later /ʃ/, then /x/), and in modern Rioplatense Spanish, where the reflex of 'll', merged with 'y', is pronounced [ʒ] (zheísmo). Outside Spanish the change is rare.

examples.note: Early fricativization of palatal /ʎ/ from Vulgar Latin -LJ-, -C'L-, -G'L- to /ʒ/; the sound later devoiced to /ʃ/ and backed to modern /x/.
Same development via [ʎ]; Portuguese preserves the lateral stage.
Zheísmo: historical /ʎ/ and /ʝ/ merged and are realized as [ʒ] in central and western Argentina; in Buenos Aires the sound has further devoiced to [ʃ] (sheísmo).

sources: Wikipedia. History of the Spanish language. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Spanish_language
